verdict: Rollout FAILED: the experiment ran, but val_bpb = 1.008368 did not improve on the current best 1.007697 by more than the required 0.0005 (lower is better).

insights_in_context.hint: Do not enable value embeddings on every layer; the previous all-layer VE result was not a true win over the relevant max-autotune baseline.

The sliding-window-shortening line had already plateaued, so the 256->128 change was a low-EV extrapolation whose ~0.0002 expected gain was below the 0.0005 keep-threshold; pick an experiment with a realistic chance of beating the best by more than 0.0005 instead.
Do not shorten the long-range L layers to 1024; the model still needs full 2048 context in more than the final layer, so choose a non-context-sacrificing experiment instead.
Raising Muon momentum to 0.97 hurt, so the momentum knob should not have been increased; if revisiting it, test lowering the steady-state momentum instead.

insight.hint: The experiment was executed correctly but the hypothesis was wrong: 0.95 is already the optimal Muon momentum, and both raising and lowering it degrade val_bpb, so this hyperparameter is exhausted in both directions and a future session should target a different unexplored knob (e.g. an intermediate sliding window between 128 and 256, or a re-run of the 256→128 near-miss to rule out noise).

judge.summary: The agent read the current train.py and experiment history, then chose to test the untried downward direction of the Muon momentum hyperparameter (0.95 → 0.90), since the upward direction (0.95 → 0.97) had already been tried and discarded. The implementation was a single-line change in get_muon_momentum(), altering the ramp endpoint from 0.95 to 0.90 so the steady-state momentum becomes 0.90 instead of 0.95 (ramp from 0.85 over 300 steps). The experiment was committed and run successfully: val_bpb = 1.008368, peak VRAM 25.3 GB, 1944 steps. This is worse than the current best of 1.007697 by ~0.0007, so the harness marked it a non-improvement and the experiment was discarded.
judge.feedback: There is no code bug or execution error in this attempt — the one-line change was implemented correctly, committed, and ran to completion without crashing. The 'failure' is purely a negative scientific result: the hypothesis that lowering Muon momentum below 0.95 would improve val_bpb was simply wrong. Combined with the earlier experiment showing 0.95 → 0.97 also hurts, this confirms 0.95 is at the optimum of the momentum knob and this dimension of the search space is exhausted in both directions. The only arguable shortcoming is in experiment selection: given that the most recent productive line was sliding-window shortening (1024→512 kept, 512→256 kept, 256→128 a near-miss at 1.007476 just below the 0.0005 improvement threshold), a higher-expected-value experiment might have been to probe an intermediate window (e.g. 192) or to revisit the near-miss 256→128 with a fresh run to check whether it was a noise anomaly. However, the chosen experiment was still a legitimate, untried, single-variable test, so the agent followed the rules correctly; the idea just did not pan out.
